assessment.risk_reasoning: Geomagnetic activity is currently quiet (Kp=2.0) with no NOAA scales in effect. The elevated 2MeV electron flux is mainly a satellite charging/radiation concern and does not directly drive thermospheric density increases. Although coronal holes are visible on the disk and could generate high-speed streams later in the period, there is no confirmed Earth-directed CME or forecast geomagnetic storm to significantly enhance LEO drag over the next 72 hours.

report.subject: ESCALATION: TEN-KOH (43677) vs YAOGAN-30 09A (48423) conjunction at 2026-10-25T06:19:38Z — split model votes, unknown propulsion
report.body: At 2026-10-25T03:19:38Z (now) we have a conjunction with NORAD 48423 (YAOGAN-30 09A) at TCA 2026-10-25T06:19:38Z (3.0 h). Miss distance 1.159 km, relative speed 13.92 km/s. Pc = 6.02e-06 (green) computed with assumed covariance from public TLE (age ~1 day). Sensitivity sweep shows Pc range 6.09e-12 to 1.90e-4 (green–red–yellow), not robust. Two physics-verified retrograde burn options exist: O1 (min_dv) 0.0929 m/s at 2026-10-25T03:55:57Z (lead 143.7 min, 1.5 orbits), miss after 2.0 km; O2 (latest) 0.7058 m/s at 2026-10-25T06:00:29Z (lead 19.1 min, 0.2 orbits), miss after 2.0 km. Both rescreened against 1449 objects, no new close approaches. Agent could not act because three independent model runs disagreed (REQUEST_PRECISE_DATA, COORDINATE, MONITOR — one vote each) and our propulsion status is unknown (no unit-specific source confirming TEN-KOH can maneuver). Policy forbids maneuver with unverified propulsion. Other operator (China) capability also unknown. Deadline for upload is latest feasible burn (O2 at 2026-10-25T06:00:29Z) minus 30 min = 2026-10-25T05:30:29Z. Need decision: verify propulsion, obtain precise ephemeris, or accept monitor.
